rationale: I went and looked, at the size the thing actually ships at. shots/mgr105-1200-day.png, seed 42, day 4 10:36, clear early summer: the town above the lane is dense and finished, and the bottom fifth of the picture is dead. Two separate faults, both in the band #100 built, and I measured both on HEAD rather than guessing. (1) The black bar under the picture is not the apron and not unpainted canvas - it is drawSill() itself, filling #0a0806 flat over the strip below sillTop(). Sampled below sillTop at three viewports and three hours, min luma == max luma == mean, exactly: 8.4 by day, 6.2 at dusk, 3.0 at night, zero pixels above luma 20 in 42,624 / 62,628 / 6,358. The sill's lit front edge, its two geranium pots and its cup are silhouetted in rgba(9,8,6) against a #0a0806 ground - under one luma unit of contrast. The whole framing conceit of the piece, the thing the fourth domain is named after, renders as a bar. That is b105. (2) Directly above it, the near roof is the largest single object in the frame (13.8% of a desktop picture, 21.7% of a phone, per #100) and NOTHING LIVES ON IT - not by oversight but by construction: the bed CA, the item sort, the seed scatter and every spawner bound their y loops at LN_WALK_S 79, and catA is pinned to the lane at x -2..66. It has a ridge, two light wells, a dormer per house, party walls, stacks and moss, and no tenant. That is b106, the bet, and it is where c151 has been pointing since #99. The rest balance the grid on cues that a worker already measured and that name their own fix: b107 takes c143 and c152 together, because both reduce to one thing (#101's own words - a far-end stay that clears by 03h needs an EARLIER far-side source, not better pricing), and it is the third pass those two have survived; b108 is c142's thin gardener in the courtyard, 9 back and the title object; b109 is c146's dawn re-key, small but sitting on the morning lapse hour that is one tap away. This is RUNG 2 and I am calling it that rather than dressing it up: the frontier right now is genuinely a deepen, the two spatial and structural rungs were spent at #99 (4b) and #94 (6), and the ladder's own note is that rung 2 is usually the highest-yield move. It is the first rung<=2 pass in three, so the rule is not binding - but it binds the next one, and if the batch after this also wants rung 2 it must climb instead.
